fam_perfect_gas_pressure: The gas constant is the fixed value R = 0.0820573661 L·atm/(mol·K), used exactly as written with no further rounding.
Pressure is p = n x R x T / V computed as a single Decimal expression at 60 significant digits, with no intermediate rounding of nR or nRT.
The final pressure is returned at full working precision with no quantize step, so it is not rounded to 4 decimal places or any other place value.
Volume is converted exactly to litres before use: m3 x 1000, dm3 and litre x 1, mL, cm3 and cc x 0.001, microlitre x 0.000001.
Amount is converted exactly to mol: mol x 1, kmol x 1000, mmol x 0.001, umol x 0.000001, with number words read as integers.
Celsius converts to kelvin by adding exactly 273.15, not 273.
Fahrenheit converts to kelvin as (F + 459.67) x 5 / 9 and Rankine as R x 5 / 9, with the division carried at 60 significant digits.
A temperature given in kelvin is used unchanged.
Amount, volume and absolute temperature must be strictly greater than zero; a value equal to zero or below raises an error, so zero is excluded.
Numeric text goes straight into Decimal from the string with no float conversion, and comma digit-group separators are stripped before parsing.
The SI cross-check is a separate returned value that does not feed the primary answer: volume in m3 is litres / 1000, then p = n x 8.314 x T / V_m3 in Pa, then divided by 101325 Pa per atm.
The cross-check uses R = 8.314 J/(mol·K) and 101325 Pa per atm, not the L·atm gas constant used for the primary answer.
The relative difference returned by the cross-check is (cross-check pressure - primary pressure) / primary pressure, returned unrounded.
fam_ddb_book_value: Money text parsing strips the dollar sign, commas, and the words usd, dollar, and dollars, then multiplies the number exactly by its scale word: k or thousand = 1000; m, mn, or million = 1000000; b, bn, or billion = 1000000000; no word = 1.
Cost and salvage are kept as exact decimals at parse time with no rounding.
Year counts are read as whole numbers: the words years, yrs, and yr are dropped, hyphens become spaces, and number words are summed (for example twenty five = 25).
The code raises an error unless cost is strictly greater than salvage, useful life is at least 2 years, and target year is at least 0.
The DDB rate is 2 divided by useful life in years, held as an exact fraction (for example 2/10 = 20 percent, or 2/3 for a 3-year life) and not rounded to a percent.
Each year's depreciation is the exact rate times the opening book value, computed at 60 significant digits, with no rounding to cents or any other unit.
The salvage floor is a cap, not a switch: if rate times opening book would take closing book below salvage, depreciation is set to opening book minus salvage, so the book lands exactly on salvage.
Once opening book is at or below salvage, depreciation is zero for that year and every later year; the code never switches to straight-line.
Useful life does not stop depreciation: years beyond the useful life keep applying DDB, limited only by the salvage floor.
The year loop runs years 1 through the target year inclusive, so the target year's depreciation is included; a target year of 0 returns the cost unchanged.
Closing book value is opening book value minus that year's depreciation, carried at 60 significant digits with no intermediate rounding.
The only rounding step is the final one: the end-of-target-year book value is rounded to the nearest cent with ROUND_HALF_UP (ties away from zero).
The reported result is a plain decimal in dollars with exactly two decimal places, with no thousands separator, currency symbol, or unit suffix.
